speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs (a) how many cases of fake bulk order scams impersonating SAF personnel have been reported since May 2025; (b) what measures are being taken to protect small businesses from such fraud; and (c) whether additional safeguards, outreach, or penalties are planned to deter impersonation scams targeting SAF’s reputation.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs): Mr Speaker, my reply will also address Question Nos 10 and 12 for written answer in today’s Order Paper filed by Mr Alex Yeo and Mr Zhulkarnain Adbul Rahim respectively.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: In some cases, nearer the delivery date, the scammers would request for additional items which the businesses do not carry or are unable to fulfil at short notice.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: The fake suppliers are part of the same scam syndicate and will deceive the victim into making payment, without delivering the actual items.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: Victims often only realise they have been scammed when the bulk order is not collected.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: The Police take a tough stance against scammers and their mules, including those who allow their bank accounts to be used to receive the scam proceeds.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: They may face imprisonment terms of up to 10 years.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: Investigations against the other suspects are currently ongoing.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: As much as the Police will take a firm stance against such cases and also do more in public education efforts, it is often not possible for the Police to protect all businesses and the public from all forms of scams and frauds.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: The criminals will also constantly devise new ways and approaches to hook and scam the victims.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: In this case, we also seek the public's support, including businesses and merchants, to be discerning and vigilant.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam
text: If in doubt, please call the ScamShield Helpline at 1799.

speaker: Mr Jackson Lam (Nee Soon)
text: Can I ask whether the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) is working with other agencies to develop verification tools or secure channels for our business owners to verify the authenticity of the orders, when orders are made?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: As mentioned in my reply, it is often not possible for the Police to fully protect the businesses and the public from all forms of fraud and scams.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Businesses should verify their identities of the people they are transacting with.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: For example, if the person claims to be a Government official, who wishes to make a bulk order for an event, businesses can consider asking for the order to be sent via an official email address, always ending with "gov.sg".

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: If in doubt, businesses can approach the relevant Government agencies or its officers using the contact details found on the official Singapore Government Directory.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Businesses should also check for reviews of suppliers to establish their legitimacy before committing to a purchase or pay only upon delivery of goods.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: If in doubt, businesses can also check the legitimacy of suspicious messages, phone numbers and website links via the ScamShield app or calling the helpline at 1799.

speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
text: Can I just ask a supplementary question to the Minister of State?

speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
text: Apart from the investigations with regard to restaurants, have the Police made any headway in their investigations towards the even smaller food and beverage outlets, like the hawkers who had been scammed by these fake bulk orders?

speaker: Mr Alex Yeo (Potong Pasir)
text: And if there is, can the Minister of State share more details about the intent of these perpetrators and who they are?

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: In terms of whether the case comes from a restaurant, or it comes from a hawker centre, I think all these are fake bulk order scams and all the cases are currently under investigation.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: As and when we do have details and conclusions from the investigations, we will make them public, especially if it is in the public interest.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Perhaps the question is also about whether we have an increasing or growing fake bulk order scam situation in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: But since May 2025, the Police have seen a recent re-emergence of this kind of scams, in this case, including the impersonation of SAF personnel and teachers from academic institutions.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Over the last four months, the Police have received at least 45 fake bulk order scam reports, which include six reports involving SAF personnel.
